newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels promise more releases if allowed contact.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels promise more releases if allowed contact.

text.p: Marxist rebels holding around 360 hostages in the Japanese embassy residence said on Friday night they would release another "significant" number of captives if the Peruvian government allowed them to talk to their jailed comrades.
In a statement read to reporters by a freed captive, the guerrillas also reiterated their desire for a peaceful, negotiated end to the crisis.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels sent their communication with a group of 38 hostages they set free from the residence on Friday night.
In the statement, the guerrillas complained about the government's hardline stance on the crisis and said they were being wrongly branded as assassins.

The group said they were standing firm on their demands for the freeing from jail of more than 400 MRTA colleagues and warned authorities not to take the hostage releases so far as a sign of weakness.
The rebels also bemoaned the government's continued refusal to restore electricity, running water and telephone services to the besieged building.
